system.name: TAVAE (VAE with adaptable priors)
system.one_liner: A VAE whose natural-image prior is swapped for a task prior explains contextual modulation of V1 responses in mice trained on a Go/NoGo task.

content.variant_note: eight lettered panels: mouse setup and stimuli, recorded data, a VAE vs TAVAE cartoon with latent and prior pictures, and model responses that echo the recorded profile
content.argues: An adaptable-prior VAE (TAVAE) that swaps the natural prior for a task prior reproduces how task training reshapes V1 population responses to the Go stimulus.
content.subject: Mouse Go/NoGo experiment, recorded V1 population responses, the VAE-to-TAVAE change, the task prior and simulated responses.

encoding.color_means: Green = trained mice (d) and task prior (h), light blue = naive mice (d) and natural prior (h); in b, green = Go and red = NoGo. In e, dark orange = VAE recognition model, pale orange = generative model (reused), mint = TAVAE recognition model; grey = x, z, x̂. Viridis = response size (c) and posterior density (f).
encoding.line_style_means: Dashed lines mark stimulus orientations (thin green at 45° in d, thick grey at 45° and 135° in h); translucent bands around the lines show spread (not defined in the figure).
encoding.shape_means: Trapezoids = recognition and generative models (narrow at z, wide at x and x̂); tall grey rectangles = x, z, x̂; square thumbnails = gratings; coloured frames = Go and NoGo rows.
encoding.marker_means: Lowercase letters a-h name the panels; D1-D6 name the test days; the degree values are stimulus orientations.
encoding.emphasis: The recorded profile (d) and the model profile (h) share axes and colours, so the match reads by eye; the mint trapezoid is the only new colour in e and the yellow hot spot is the one bright item in c.
reusable_patterns: experiment panels in the top row and model panels in the bottom row, with the recorded profile and the simulated profile on the same axes and colours
stimulus strip with one thumbnail per session and its parameter in coloured text, in framed Go and NoGo rows

dashed horizontal reference lines at the stimulus orientation across line plots
receptive-field thumbnails at the axis ends of a latent-space sketch to show what each latent encodes
apparatus illustration with plain text labels as the setup panel

lessons.what_to_learn: Put experiment panels (setup, stimuli, recorded map and profile) over model panels (cartoon, latent picture, prior, simulated profile) and give the recorded and the simulated profile the same axes and colours so the match is checked by eye. Draw baseline and proposed model as two rows of the same trapezoids, keeping the colour of the unchanged block and nesting the old block inside the new.

evidence: The TAVAE generative model component of VAE (pale orange) is reused in TAVAE
the NoGo stimulus gradually converged to the Go stimulus (Fig. 1b)

summary: TAVAE is a variational autoencoder whose prior can be swapped for a task prior, used to explain how learning a Go/NoGo orientation task changes responses in mouse primary visual cortex. Figure 1 is an eight-panel composite. The top row covers the experiment: a rig illustration (a), the Go (45°) and NoGo gratings across training and six test days (b), a population response heat map for the Go stimulus (c) and the trained-versus-naive response profile (d). The bottom row covers the model: a trapezoid cartoon of VAE and TAVAE, the latter reusing the pale-orange generative model and framing the old recognition model inside a mint one (e), a latent posterior map with receptive fields (f), the task prior (g) and model responses with task and natural priors (h), drawn like d.
summary_zh: TAVAE 是带可调先验的 VAE，用来解释小鼠视觉皮层在 Go/NoGo 任务中的响应变化。图 1 的 a 到 h 面板：上排为实验装置、刺激、记录热图与响应曲线，下排为 VAE/TAVAE 示意、潜变量后验、任务先验和模型响应。
notes: The pre-screen kinds (concept-schematic, model-anatomy) were kept; side-by-side-contrast was added for d vs h and VAE vs TAVAE. The left quarter of the preview is blank canvas padding. The bitmap or vector status of panel a and of the curve in g was inferred from the SVG image list (the g curve looks like a placed bitmap rotated 90 degrees).
